items.title: Ten years after demonetisation, In India cash is still king
items.summary: Ten years after Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the withdrawal of Rs 500 and Rs 1,000 notes, questions remain about whether demonetisation achieved its stated objectives. While digital payments have grown rapidly, cash continues to play a major role in the economy. The impact on black money, counterfeit currency and informal workers also remains contested. Announcing the decision to demonetise Rs 500 and Rs 1000 currency notes, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on November 8, 2016 said : “In a country’s history, there come moments when every person feels he too should be part of that moment, that he too should make his contribution to the country’s progress. Such moments come but rarely. Now, we again have an opportunity where every citizen can join this mahayajna against the ills of corruption, black money and fake notes. The more help you give in this campaign, the more successful it will be.” "The magnitude of cash in circulation is directly linked to the level of corruption," the PM had stated. items.title: SC raises alarm over elephants transferred hastily to Tamil Nadu from Assam
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday (November 5) expressed concern over the allegedly hurried inter-state transfer of captive elephants, including one that was transported nearly 3,000 km to Chennai within nine days, raising questions about whether the statutory procedures governing such movements had been followed, The Print reported. According to the report, a bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi was hearing a petition filed by the NGO People for Cattle in India, which challenged the procedure followed by authorities for the transfer of these captive elephants. According to a social media post on X by Bar and Bench , senior advocate Meenakshi Arora, appearing for the petitioner, told the court that the statutory framework governing the inter-state movement of captive elephants requires several stages of verification, clearances and consultations, a process that ordinarily takes a minimum of around 50 days. However, in this case, the transfer request was made on September 4 and the elephant reached Chennai by September 13, covering a distance of nearly 3,000 kms in just nine days, she said.
